Each entry contains correct role, number, id, version fields matching source YAML
deep_agents.agent_name equals the da_file_name stem (falling back to cc_file_name if absent)
Running the script twice with unchanged YAML produces identical output

summary: Added a post-build name-mapping generation step to scripts/build-personas.js. After the existing version-sync block, the script reads all 9 ledger persona YAML files from personas/ledger/src/meta/, extracts role/number/id/version/vs_file_name/cc_file_name/da_file_name via a lightweight inline scalar parser (no new npm dependencies), computes per-target agent_name values, and writes personas/name-mapping.json sorted by number. The step is guarded by !CHECK so --check/--dry-run modes skip it entirely.

comments.note: scripts/build-personas.js inline YAML scalar parser is intentionally minimal (only top-level key: value pairs). If persona YAML structure ever gains multi-line scalar values or inline tables, the parser would silently skip them. A comment documenting this limitation (and the decision to avoid js-yaml in root scripts) would help future maintainers. No action needed now.

The name-mapping generation block always calls fs.writeFileSync even when the resulting JSON would be byte-for-byte identical to the existing file. This causes an unnecessary mtime update on every build. A read-then-compare guard (like the version-sync block's pkg.version !== newVersion check) would avoid spurious file touches and keep Git diffs clean. Low-priority since builds are not frequent.

summary: All 8 acceptance criteria verified and passing. personas/name-mapping.json contains exactly 9 entries, each independently cross-checked against source YAML files. All field values (role, number, id, version, all file_name and agent_name values per target) match source data precisely. Build is idempotent (identical MD5 hash across two successive runs). --check and --dry-run modes both leave the file untouched (mtime unchanged). No new npm dependencies introduced at root level. Edge: --dry-run alias correctly shares the CHECK guard. Edge: da_file_name fallback to cc_file_name is correctly implemented though untested by current data.

comments.note: The da_file_name fallback path (da_file_name || cc_file_name) is correctly implemented but never exercised by current data since all 9 persona YAMLs define da_file_name. If a future persona omits it, the fallback will silently activate — which is correct behaviour per AC5.
--dry-run alias was also verified to skip name-mapping.json generation (same CHECK guard as --check). Both flags leave the file mtime unchanged.

summary: Code review PASS with four Fix-Forward improvements applied. The name-mapping generation logic in scripts/build-personas.js is clean, focused, and correct for all current data. Fix-Forward changes: (1) Added _shared.yaml default_version fallback — the plan specified it but it was omitted; future personas omitting `version` would have produced `vundefined` without this guard. (2) Expanded parseYamlScalars JSDoc to document the trailing-inline-comment limitation, as flagged by the Developer pipeline comment. (3) Added maintenance comment on PERSONA_FILES noting sync dependency with workflow-manifest.json. (4) Extracted `number` and `version` as local variables before the return statement to eliminate the data.number string/number inconsistency in the template literal. All four changes verified non-behavioral: name-mapping.json diff is empty after full rebuild.

comments.note: Added `_shared.yaml` default_version fallback. Before the mapping.map() call, the script now reads `_shared.yaml` via parseYamlScalars and derives DEFAULT_VERSION. Each persona entry uses `data.version || DEFAULT_VERSION`. The plan described this guard; the implementation omitted it. Silent `vundefined` output would have broken VS Code agent names for any future persona added without an explicit version field.

Expanded parseYamlScalars JSDoc to document that trailing inline YAML comments are not stripped (e.g. `role: Developer # note` -> `"Developer # note"`). Developer had flagged this as an improvement in the implementation pipeline. Applied directly as a code comment.

Added two-line maintenance comment above the PERSONA_FILES constant noting it must stay in sync with the 9 ledger roles in shared/workflow-manifest.json and must be updated when a new persona is added.

Extracted `number = Number(data.number)` and `version = data.version || DEFAULT_VERSION` as local variables before the return statement. Eliminates the string/number inconsistency where data.number (string) was used in the agent_name template literal while Number(data.number) was used in the returned object property. Non-behavioral since string interpolation of '1' and 1 both produce '1'.
